claim_checks.claim: Edge-triggered (ET), with EPOLLET
claim_checks.page_says: EPOLLET Requests edge-triggered notification for the associated file descriptor.

claim_checks.claim: Several widely used event loops register with ET: the Go runtime
claim_checks.page_says: ev.Events = linux.EPOLLIN | linux.EPOLLOUT | linux.EPOLLRDHUP | linux.EPOLLET
claim_checks.note: The source shows Go registering with EPOLLET. The characterization 'widely used' is not in the page; no cited source supports it.

claim_checks.claim: Wakeup callback: the function epoll hooks onto each watched file's wait queue
claim_checks.page_says: This is the callback that is used to add our wait queue to the target file wakeup lists. ... init_waitqueue_func_entry(&pwq->wait, ep_poll_callback);

claim_checks.claim: EAGAIN concrete artifact: read(4096) = -1 (Resource temporarily unavailable)
claim_checks.page_says: probe-01 printed 'read(4096) = -1 (Resource temporarily unavailable)'; no page is cited
claim_checks.note: probe-01 is valid and passes, but this is role 2, where a probe alone supports nothing. pipe.c (cached, not cited here) shows a nonblocking empty-pipe read returning -EAGAIN.

claim_checks.claim: Thundering herd: 4 of 4 threads woken by one write in LT mode
claim_checks.page_says: probe-10 printed '[T10-LT] ... threads that returned with an event: 4 of 4'; no page is cited
claim_checks.note: probe-10 is valid (repeat=3, all pass), but role 2 takes no probe-only support. The claim also carries no version.

claim_checks.section: ## 3. The actors and their data structures
claim_checks.claim: epoll instance (struct eventpoll): stores registrations via a red-black tree of epitems and queues ready ones via the ready list
claim_checks.page_says: /* RB tree root used to store monitored fd structs */ struct rb_root_cached rbr; ... /* List of ready file descriptors */ struct list_head rdllist;

claim_checks.section: ## 3. The actors and their data structures
claim_checks.claim: Each registration costs roughly 160 bytes on a 64-bit kernel, and max_user_watches caps the total per user
claim_checks.page_says: Each registered file descriptor costs roughly 90 bytes on a 32-bit kernel, and roughly 160 bytes on a 64-bit kernel.
claim_checks.note: The same paragraph says 'The limit is per real user ID.'

claim_checks.claim: When EPOLLIN/EPOLLOUT is unset, that direction is ignored: wakeups whose bits do not overlap the mask are dropped by the callback
claim_checks.page_says: if (pollflags && !(pollflags & epi->event.events)) goto out_unlock;
claim_checks.note: 'Wakeups whose bits' presupposes a keyed wakeup. §5 step 4 states the keyless case.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLRDHUP since 2.6.17
claim_checks.page_says: EPOLLRDHUP (since Linux 2.6.17)

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE unset: all instances are woken
claim_checks.page_says: The default in this scenario (when EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is not set) is for all epoll file descriptors to receive an event.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE unset: all instances are woken (probe mark)
claim_checks.page_says: The default in this scenario (when EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is not set) is for all epoll file descriptors to receive an event.
claim_checks.note: probe-11 is valid and passes 3 runs, but in role 5 a probe supports nothing. The claim stands on [^ctl], judged together.

claim_checks.claim: data field: opaque value returned with each event, from the latest ADD or MOD
claim_checks.page_says: The data field of each returned epoll_event structure contains the same data as was specified in the most recent call to epoll_ctl(2) (EPOLL_CTL_ADD, EPOLL_CTL_MOD)

claim_checks.claim: If a harvest is running, puts the epitem on the overflow list; otherwise links it on the ready list only if it is not already linked
claim_checks.page_says: if (ep_is_scanning(ep)) { if (!epi_on_ovflist(epi)) { ... } else if (!ep_is_linked(epi)) { /* In the usual case, add event to ready list. */

claim_checks.claim: That is why several writes before one epoll_wait produce one event
claim_checks.page_says: If more than one event occurs between epoll_wait(2) calls, are they combined or reported separately? They will be combined.
claim_checks.note: The page carries the claim. probe-03 (valid, pass) corroborates: 'after 3 writes -> 1 event(s)', read returns 3.

claim_checks.claim: epoll_wait: if the ready list is empty, the thread adds itself to the instance's wait queue as an exclusive waiter and sleeps
claim_checks.page_says: eavail = ep_events_available(ep); if (!eavail) __add_wait_queue_exclusive(&ep->wq, &wait); ... return !list_empty_careful(&ep->rdllist) || ep_is_scanning(ep) ||
claim_checks.note: Dropped condition: the thread sleeps only when no events are available, which also requires that no harvest (scan) is in progress, not just an empty ready list.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLONESHOT: reduces the mask to its private bits, so later callbacks ignore the item until EPOLL_CTL_MOD
claim_checks.page_says: if (epi->event.events & EPOLLONESHOT) { epi->event.events &= EP_PRIVATE_BITS;
claim_checks.note: The callback comment adds: 'EPOLLONESHOT bit that disables the descriptor when an event is received, until the next EPOLL_CTL_MOD will be issued.'

claim_checks.claim: Everything else that makes ET 'feel' different follows from that branch, plus one side channel: the mask travels to the driver as the poll key, and the pipe driver reads it
claim_checks.page_says: wait && (wait->_key & EPOLLET) && unlikely(!READ_ONCE(pipe->pseudo_edgetrigger))) WRITE_ONCE(pipe->pseudo_edgetrigger, true);
claim_checks.note: pipe.c backs the side channel, and eventpoll.c line 'pt->_key = epi->event.events' backs the key. No page says that everything else follows from the one branch and that this is the only side channel. That universal is the doc's own inference, and §14 does not list it as synthesis.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: 2048 bytes arrive; the app reads 1024 and waits again: No event; 1024 bytes stranded (T1; the man page's pipe example)
claim_checks.page_says: the call to epoll_wait(2) done in step 5 will probably hang despite the available data still present in the file input buffer
claim_checks.note: The man page hedges ('will probably hang', 'might block indefinitely'); the row states 'No event' plainly. probe-01 (valid, pass) observed 0 events twice on Linux 7.2.12, but a probe does not excuse a raised modal on the page it cites.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: New data while old data is still unread: new event on a pipe, an AF_UNIX stream socket and TCP over loopback (Linux 7.2.12), T4
claim_checks.page_says: after 2nd byte (1st still unread) -> 1 event(s) [data=1 IN] (printed for pipe, AF_UNIX stream socketpair and TCP over loopback)
claim_checks.note: Valid probe (checks 1, 0, 1 events per kind), pass. The claim is worded as an observation with its kernel version.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: EPOLLET | EPOLLONESHOT, second write before re-arm: no event until EPOLL_CTL_MOD; the mask is disabled after delivery
claim_checks.page_says: the file descriptor is disabled in the interest list and no other events will be reported by the epoll interface. The user must call epoll_ctl() with EPOLL_CTL_MOD to rearm
claim_checks.note: probe-07 (valid, pass) corroborates.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: Pipe filled to EAGAIN (65536 bytes), reader takes 1 byte: no EPOLLOUT (T8)
claim_checks.page_says: wrote 65536 bytes before write() failed with Resource temporarily unavailable ... after reading 1 byte -> 0 event(s)
claim_checks.note: Valid probe, pass. The row's rule is carried by the cited pages: pipe.c wakes writers only when a fully consumed buffer leaves a full pipe ('wake_writer |= pipe_full(...)'), and pipe(7) gives '65,536 bytes in a system with a page size of 4096 bytes'.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: 2019-12-07, Linus Torvalds, commit 1b6b26ae7053 'pipe: fix and clarify pipe write wakeup logic': a pipe write now wakes readers only if the pipe was empty before
claim_checks.page_says: Date: Sat Dec 7 12:14:28 2019 -0800 / now we only wake up a reader of a pipe when we add data to it AND IT WAS EMPTY BEFORE.
claim_checks.note: Grounded only with [^linus2020] (the wake rule), a Rank 6 source cited in a role 3 section: KB-15 breach, recorded separately. [^c3a34] (rank 4) describes the same rule and could replace it.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: It ships in Linux 5.5
claim_checks.page_says: Between Linux 5.4 and 5.5 a regression was introduced in the operation of the epoll EPOLLET flag.
claim_checks.note: Kerrisk bisects the regression to that commit, so the commit landed between 5.4 and 5.5.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: realm-core expected an ET event on every write, using a pipe it does not drain until it fills
claim_checks.page_says: The library uses a similar notification mechanism as GNU Make but it never drains the pipe until it is full.
claim_checks.note: The commit also says the libraries 'expected "edge triggered" be to "any new write will trigger it"'.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: io_uring multishot polls set EPOLLET and get the same behaviour
claim_checks.page_says: Currently io_uring sets EPOLLET for multishot polls, so it gets the same behaviour.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: Drain until EAGAIN, and a missing 'per-write' event cannot hurt you
claim_checks.page_says: You must consider it ready until the next (nonblocking) read/write yields EAGAIN.
claim_checks.note: epoll(7) offers draining as 'the suggested way' to 'avoid stalls'. It never says a missing per-write event cannot hurt; the same page says 'an event will be generated upon each receipt of a chunk of data'. 'Cannot' raises the page's suggestion to a guarantee.

claim_checks.section: ## 7. Worked example: a correct ET loop, one full pass
claim_checks.claim: Budget plus an application-level ready list: draining a very busy fd can starve the others; the man page suggests keeping your own ready list
claim_checks.page_says: it is possible that by trying to drain it the other files will not get processed causing starvation. ... The solution is to maintain a ready list
claim_checks.note: The page's 'round robin amongst all the ready files' covers the budget.

claim_checks.claim: Second thread on the same instance: ET, one thread wakes per trigger; LT, the re-queued item makes the scan end with a non-empty list, which wakes the next thread (4 of 4 woke)
claim_checks.page_says: if (!list_empty(&ep->rdllist)) { if (waitqueue_active(&ep->wq)) wake_up(&ep->wq); } / probe-10: ET '1 of 4', LT '4 of 4'
claim_checks.note: Taken as the row's last cell (the bare '✅[^src]' after the probe mark). eventpoll.c backs the mechanism (exclusive waiters, LT re-queue, end-of-scan wake). The count '4 of 4 woke' comes from the probe alone and is worded as a past observation; its version (7.2.12) is given only in §13.

claim_checks.claim: Another epoll instance watches the same file: all instances wake (4 of 4), unless all used EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (1 of 4 woke)
claim_checks.page_says: instances that returned with an event: 4 of 4 / instances that returned with an event: 1 of 4
claim_checks.note: probe-11 is valid and passes (repeat=3), but the cell rests on it alone and is worded as a rule with no version. The rule's implied mixed case (some instances exclusive, so all wake) goes beyond the probe, and epoll_ctl(2) (cached, not cited here) contradicts it: 'events will be provided to all epoll instances that did not specify EPOLLEXCLUSIVE, and at least one of the epoll instances that did'.

claim_checks.claim: Marek Majkowski describes the general problem, and recommends EPOLL_CTL_DEL before every close
claim_checks.page_says: You always must always explicitly call epoll_ctl(EPOLL_CTL_DEL) before calling close().
claim_checks.note: Grounded, but [^majek2] is Rank 6 cited in a role 3 section: KB-15 breach, recorded separately.

claim_checks.claim: The ENOENT case is not a dead end: dup2(B, A) recreates fd number A on the same description, and EPOLL_CTL_DEL on A then succeeds
claim_checks.page_says: dup2(B, A), then DEL on A -> 0 (ok)
claim_checks.note: probe-13 is valid and passes, but the sentence rests on it alone and is worded as a general rule with no version (Linux 7.2.12). epoll(7)'s key rule ('the combination of the file descriptor number and the open file description') would back it but is not cited in this sentence.

claim_checks.section: ## 9. Multiple threads and multiple epoll instances
claim_checks.claim: Remedy: EPOLLET | EPOLLONESHOT; the handling thread re-arms with EPOLL_CTL_MOD when done
claim_checks.page_says: The correct solution is to use EPOLLONESHOT and re-arm the file descriptor manually.
claim_checks.note: Rank 6 in role 6 is allowed.

claim_checks.section: ## 9. Multiple threads and multiple epoll instances
claim_checks.claim: Remedy for the accept herd: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (Linux 4.5+)
claim_checks.page_says: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (since Linux 4.5) ... EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is thus useful for avoiding thundering herd problems in certain scenarios.

claim_checks.section: ## 9. Multiple threads and multiple epoll instances
claim_checks.claim: That thread may keep draining the accept queue while the others idle, so the load is not spread
claim_checks.page_says: In this case all the connections will be received by Thread A and load balancing won't be achieved.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLET | EPOLLONESHOT: one owner per event
claim_checks.page_says: This is the only way to guarantee that the data will be delivered to only one thread and avoid race conditions.

claim_checks.claim: The closest BSD analogue is kqueue's EV_CLEAR, which resets an event's state after it is retrieved, and EV_DISPATCH disables the event source after delivery, much like EPOLLONESHOT
claim_checks.page_says: EV_CLEAR Reset the state of the event after it is retrieved by the user. ... EV_DISPATCH Disable the event source immediately after delivery of an event.
claim_checks.note: The flag definitions are entailed. 'Closest BSD analogue' and 'much like EPOLLONESHOT' are not in the page; the doc's next sentence admits the mapping is its own, yet the ✅ covers it.

claim_checks.claim: mio's docs require repeating the operation until WouldBlock and warn of spurious events
claim_checks.page_says: Once a readiness event is received, the corresponding operation must be performed repeatedly until it returns WouldBlock.
claim_checks.note: The Spurious events section: 'Poll::poll may return readiness events even if the associated event source is not actually ready.'

claim_checks.claim: io_uring multishot poll: ET semantics reach beyond epoll: pipes treat it the same way
claim_checks.page_says: Currently io_uring sets EPOLLET for multishot polls, so it gets the same behaviour.

claim_checks.claim: Connection hangs with bytes in its receive buffer; cause one read per event in ET mode; fix read until EAGAIN (or a short read on a stream fd)
claim_checks.page_says: You must consider it ready until the next (nonblocking) read/write yields EAGAIN.
claim_checks.note: The short-read shortcut is on the same page: 'if you call read(2) by asking to read a certain amount of data and read(2) returns a lower number of bytes, you can be sure of having exhausted the read I/O space'.

claim_checks.claim: One busy client starves the others; fix: a per-fd budget plus an application ready list
claim_checks.page_says: The solution is to maintain a ready list and mark the file descriptor as ready in its associated data structure ... still round robin amongst all the ready files.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLOUT arrives late: the driver wakes writers only past a threshold (T8)
claim_checks.page_says: reader consumed 4096 of 65536 bytes -> 1 event(s) [OUT] / reader consumed 151552 of 196608 bytes -> 1 event(s) [OUT]
claim_checks.note: Valid probe, pass.

claim_checks.claim: The threshold for AF_UNIX: a quarter of the socket send buffer
claim_checks.page_says: (refcount_read(&sk->sk_wmem_alloc) << 2) <= READ_ONCE(sk->sk_sndbuf);
claim_checks.note: unix_write_space() wakes waiters only when unix_writable() holds.

claim_checks.claim: Events arrive for an fd already closed because a dup or fork keeps the description alive; fix EPOLL_CTL_DEL before close; recover with dup2 onto the old number, then delete
claim_checks.page_says: events may be reported for that file descriptor if other file descriptors referring to the same underlying file description remain open.
claim_checks.note: Judged together: epoll(7) gives the cause, majek2 gives DEL before close, and probe-13 (valid, pass) shows the dup2 recovery. epoll(7)'s own fix is DEL 'before it is duplicated'.

claim_checks.claim: More ready fds than maxevents: nothing is lost; undelivered items stay queued and later calls round-robin
claim_checks.page_says: If more than n file descriptors are ready when epoll_wait() is called, then successive epoll_wait() calls will round robin through the set of ready file descriptors.
claim_checks.note: probe-12 (valid, pass) corroborates: data 10, 11, 12, then 0.

claim_checks.claim: The refined doc's row 'several threads woken for one event' holds for level-triggered registrations; with EPOLLET, one thread wakes per trigger (T10)
claim_checks.page_says: just one of the threads (or processes) is awoken from epoll_wait(2).
claim_checks.note: Judged as role 3 (it restates §8/§9). epoll(7) backs the ET half. The LT half ('holds for level-triggered registrations') rests on probe-10 alone, a no-reader run on Linux 7.2.12, and is worded as a general rule with no version.

patch_instructions.action: Step 1: replace [^linus2020] with [^c3a34], which states the same rule ('if the pipe already had data in it before the write, there was no point in trying to wake up a reader'). Step 3: move Linus's reply to a role-6 row in §12 (misconception: 'a write to a readable pipe is no edge'), with [^linus2020] marked Rank 6, or drop it from role 3.

patch_instructions.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
patch_instructions.action: In §6.3, quote epoll(7): 'an event will be generated upon each receipt of a chunk of data' ✅[^epoll7]. Reword step 5 so the doc's own voice no longer says realm-core 'relied on behaviour they should not have'; attribute it instead ('the commit calls it misuse' ✅[^c3a34]). Add a role-6 row in §12 recording the disagreement: epoll(7) (rank 1) promises per-chunk events, while Linus (rank 6) and the commit (rank 4) call them no edge. Mainline pipe.c (rank 1) keeps per-write wakeups for EPOLLET readers ('Legacy epoll(EPOLLET) users depend on historical per-write wakeups'), and draining to EAGAIN is safe either way.
